games.note: Released weeks after Threes with powers-of-two tiles and the tagline 'No need to pay for Threes'; it directly sparked 2048.

games.title: Happy Farm
games.note: Shanghai studio 5 Minutes drew 23 million daily players in China with timed crops and playful neighbor crop-stealing.

games.title: Farm Town
games.note: Facebook farming hit launched four months before FarmVille, where friends met in town to hire harvest helpers.

games.title: Backyard Monsters
games.note: Facebook base-building strategy game where players fortified a yard with towers, hatched monsters and raided rivals.

games.title: Helicopter Game
games.note: One-button Flash game by Simon Eriksson on Seethru.co.uk where holding the mouse lifts a helicopter through caves.

games.title: Piou Piou vs. Cactus
games.note: French mobile game by Kek where tapping flaps a small yellow bird past rows of green cacti.

games.title: Klondike
games.note: Single-player patience card game named after the Klondike Gold Rush and recorded in Hoyle's Games in 1907.

games.title: Jotto
games.note: Paper-and-pencil deduction game from 1955 where two players guess secret five-letter words from letter-overlap counts.

games.title: Mastermind
games.note: Code-breaking peg game invented by Israeli postmaster Mordecai Meirowitz, using black and white pegs for position clues.

games.title: Full Tilt! Pinball
games.note: Three-table pre-rendered 3D pinball game whose Space Cadet table Microsoft bundled with Windows 95 Plus! and XP.

games.title: Interactive Physics
games.note: Educational 2D physics lab by David and Greg Baszucki where students ended up crashing cars and building contraptions.

updates.value: Built by Josh Wardle during 2020 for his partner Palak Shah, who trimmed the list to familiar five-letter words.
Designer Luke Muscat pitched the game at Halfbrick after watching a chef-knife infomercial slice fruit in mid-air.
Created in a few days by Hanoi developer Dong Nguyen, who pulled it at its peak in February 2014.
Built in six months by a small Supercell team in Helsinki adapting browser base-raiding strategy for touchscreens.

links.took: Swiping a four-by-four grid so every numbered tile slides at once and matching tiles merge.
links.added: Replaced multiples of three with powers of two and released the game free on mobile.

src.t: IBTimes, Origin of Threes, 1024 and 2048, Mar 2014

links.extra: Veewo's App Store listing pitched 1024 directly as a free alternative to Threes.

links.took: Sliding powers-of-two tiles across a four-by-four board until matching numbers double toward a target tile.
links.added: Doubled the target to 2048, smoothed the keyboard animations and shared the browser code free on GitHub.

src.t: Gabriele Cirulli, 2048 GitHub repository README, Mar 2014
IBTimes, Origin of Threes, 1024 and 2048, Mar 2014

links.extra: Cirulli built 2048 in a weekend after playing Veewo's 1024 and Saming's 2048, before he had played Threes.

links.took: Moving every tile on a four-by-four grid together to combine numbers without letting the board fill.
links.added: Reached millions as an unmonetized open-source browser game using powers of two via 1024.

src.t: Gabriele Cirulli, 2048 GitHub repository README, Mar 2014

links.extra: 2048's page credits 1024 by Veewo Studio and notes it is conceptually similar to Threes by Asher Vollmer.

links.took: Clearing plots, planting seasonal crops, tending livestock and checking back as harvests ripen.
links.added: Real-time crop timers on Chinese social networks, where friends help water plots or steal ripe produce.

src.t: Wikipedia: Happy Farm (5 Minutes inspired by Harvest Moon)
PC Gamer, The 5 biggest PC games in China, 2014

links.extra: 5 Minutes designed Happy Farm in Shanghai after Japanese console farming games led by Harvest Moon.

links.took: Isometric plots where timed crops wither if left unpicked, shared asynchronously with social-network friends.
links.added: Brought the social farm loop onto Facebook and added a town square to hire real-time harvest helpers.

links.took: Facebook farming plots, withering crop timers, coins-and-cash dual currency and neighbor farm visits.
links.added: Streamlined one-click planting, news-feed gift requests and Zynga cross-promotion that reached 83 million monthly players.
links.extra: Launched on Facebook in June 2009, four months after Slashkey's Farm Town.

links.took: Planting timed crops, raising animals and visiting friends' farms inside a social network.
links.added: Replaced neighbor crop-stealing with cooperative gifts, ribbons and Facebook feed viral loops.

src.t: Wikipedia: Happy Farm (citing Wired on social farm clones)

links.took: Crop timers, animal pens, neighbor help and seasonal farm decorations on Facebook.
links.added: Full 3D visuals and a crafting loop turning water, crops and animal goods into bakery recipes.

links.took: Arranging defensive towers and walls to funnel incoming waves of attackers inside a browser.
links.added: Persistent resource yards and player-versus-player monster raids at Kixeye, co-founded by Desktop TD creator Paul Preece.

src.t: Wikipedia: Desktop Tower Defense (Casual Collective / Kixeye)

links.extra: Paul Preece and David Scott's Casual Collective rebranded as Kixeye while launching Backyard Monsters.

links.took: Warcraft III popularized real-time base building, resource harvesting and custom tower-defense maps.
links.added: Asynchronous browser raids where your yard's towers defend automatically while you are offline.

links.took: Fortifying a persistent base with walls and towers, training troops on timers and raiding rivals.
links.added: Touchscreen troop-drop controls, crisp fantasy silhouettes, clan wars and brisk mobile sessions.

src.t: Lasse Louhento (Supercell), Making of Clash of Clans, PocketGamer.biz

links.extra: Product lead Lasse Louhento cited Backyard Monsters and Travian as key inspirations for Supercell's mobile strategy game.

links.took: Clash of Clans' barbarians, giants, archers and spells, built by a new cell inside Supercell.
links.added: Live head-to-head two-lane tower duels driven by an eight-card elixir deck in three-minute matches.

links.took: Supercell's small-cell studio craft, club social structure, trophy progression and three-minute mobile sessions.
links.added: Direct twin-stick arena shooting and hero supers across three-on-three objective and survival modes.

links.took: Automatic endless sprinting where a single mistimed jump ends the run and distance sets the score.
links.added: Shifted from 2D rooftops to a behind-the-back 3D path with swipe turns, slides and tilt coins.

src.t: Macworld, Behind the success of Temple Run (Keith Shepherd), 2012

links.extra: Imangi co-founder Keith Shepherd set out to bring Canabalt's one-run tension into a 3D adventure camera.

links.took: Behind-the-back 3D endless running with swipe jumps, rolls and lane switches while fleeing a pursuer.
links.added: Three clear train-track lanes without tilt steering, crash-proof hoverboards, jetpacks and world-tour cities.
links.extra: Released nine months after Temple Run by Danish studios SYBO Games and Kiloo.

links.took: Swipe-and-tilt endless fleeing along narrow temple walkways with coin magnets and score multipliers.
links.added: Curving hills, zip-lines, minecart tracks and character-specific power-ups.

links.took: Bright green warp pipes and unforgiving 8-bit obstacle spacing from Nintendo's Famicom platformer.
links.added: Reduced movement to one tap that bounces a heavy bird between endless vertical pipe gaps.

src.t: CNET, Dong Nguyen interview on Flappy Bird's Mario and paddleball roots

links.extra: Dong Nguyen grew up playing Super Mario Bros. in Hanoi and paired its look with a paddleball rhythm.

links.took: Helicopter Game popularized one-button gravity flight through endless narrow gaps where any touch ends the run.
links.added: Discrete upward hops on each screen tap rather than hold-to-climb thrust, with instant portrait restarts.

src.t: IGN, History of Flappy Bird, Sep 2024

links.took: Tapping a touchscreen to keep a round yellow bird with a big beak aloft between green hazards.
links.added: Heavier gravity, tighter vertical pipe openings and one-point-per-gap arcade tension.

src.t: Mashable, Flappy Bird and Kek's Piou Piou comparison
IGN, Flappy Bird history and Kek's later involvement, Sep 2024

links.extra: French developer Kek noted the resemblance in 2014; Dong Nguyen replied that he had not previously seen Piou Piou.

links.took: Instant-restart endless score chasing, one-touch mobile controls and shareable short runs.
links.added: Combined that endless structure with Frogger's traffic lanes, voxel mascots and fair cosmetic unlocks.

src.t: IBTimes UK, Matt Hall and Andy Sum on Crossy Road and Flappy Bird, Dec 2014

links.extra: Hipster Whale co-founder Matt Hall described Crossy Road as blending endless Flappy Bird sessions with Frogger.

links.took: Blockade popularized steering a growing line around a boxed screen without hitting walls or tails.
links.added: Single-player pellet-chasing built into millions of pocket Nokia handsets starting in 1997.

links.took: Steering an ever-lengthening snake that eats pellets and dies the moment its head strikes a body.
links.added: Hundreds of live online snakes in one arena where tiny newcomers can cut off and consume leaders.

src.t: Steve Howse, interview, Pocket Gamer, May 2016

links.extra: Solo developer Steve Howse combined classic Snake rules with Agar.io's drop-in browser multiplayer.

links.took: Drop-in browser and mobile arenas where hundreds of players eat glowing orbs to climb a live leaderboard.
links.added: Swapped Agar.io's size-wins cells for Snake's head-crash rule, letting small players topple giants.

src.t: Steve Howse, interview, Pocket Gamer, May 2016

links.took: Wii Sports Resort's Speed Slice popularized cleanly cleaving tossed fruit in mid-air with physical swings.
links.added: Direct finger-swipe blade trails on glass touchscreens, multi-fruit combos and flying bombs to dodge.

src.t: IGN, Wii Sports Resort: Speed Slice

links.extra: Luke Muscat also credited a late-night chef-knife infomercial showing pineapples sliced in mid-air.

links.took: Immediate, tactile touchscreen slicing microgames anyone can grasp in seconds.
links.added: Expanded one satisfying swipe action into a full arcade score-attack loop with juicy fruit physics.

src.t: PC Gamer, Profile of Fruit Ninja designer Luke Muscat

links.took: Klondike's seven-column tableau, alternating-color cascades, three-card draw stock and four suit foundations.
links.added: Mouse drag-and-drop card handling, automatic rule checks, pixel card backs and the bouncing victory cascade.
links.extra: Shipped with Windows 3.0 in 1990, introducing millions of PC owners to mouse drag-and-drop.

links.took: Klondike's seven-pile patience layout, alternating red-and-black sequences and Ace-to-King suit foundations.
links.added: Wes Cherry's Windows 3.0 program, Susan Kare's pixel card art and effortless digital shuffling.

links.took: A quiet, solo 52-card tabletop feel that welcomes players outside traditional strategy circles.
links.added: Poker hand scoring, rule-breaking Joker multipliers, tarot deck edits and rising blind targets.

src.t: GamesRadar+, LocalThunk on Solitaire inspiring Balatro, Mar 2025

links.extra: LocalThunk wrote that Solitaire was arguably the single most important inspiration behind Balatro's cozy card feel.

links.took: Jotto popularized deducing an opponent's hidden sequence in fixed turns using match-count clues.
links.added: Colored plastic code pegs and separate black-and-white key pegs distinguishing exact spots from misplaced colors.

links.took: Six-row deductive guessing with color-coded feedback showing exact-position hits versus misplaced matches.
links.added: Five-letter English words, one shared puzzle per day for everyone and spoiler-free emoji grids.

src.t: TechCrunch, Josh Wardle interview on Wordle's origins, Jan 2022

links.extra: Josh Wardle built his first 2013 Wordle prototype directly as a word-based take on Mastermind.

links.took: Jotto popularized testing valid five-letter English words to narrow down a hidden five-letter answer.
links.added: Per-letter green and yellow tile colors instead of a single match count, played solo once daily.

links.took: Pinball Dreams popularized realistic computer ball physics, table missions and multi-table home pinball sets.
links.added: Full-view pre-rendered 3D tables with rank promotions across Space Cadet, Skulduggery and Dragon's Keep.

links.took: Cinematronics' Space Cadet table, mission ranks, wormhole bumpers and sound effects from Full Tilt! Pinball.
links.added: Ported to Windows APIs by Dave Plummer and preinstalled for millions on Windows NT, 2000, Me and XP.
links.extra: Microsoft licensed the Space Cadet table from Maxis and Cinematronics at 640x480 resolution.

links.took: David Baszucki's open-ended physics lab where students built vehicles, ramps and crashes for fun.
links.added: 3D Lego-like blocks, Lua scripting and shared online servers where players publish games for others.

src.t: Game Developer, David Baszucki interview on Interactive Physics and Roblox, 2006
Roblox Newsroom, David Baszucki on Knowledge Revolution and Interactive Physics

links.extra: Watching kids use Interactive Physics as a toy inspired Baszucki and Erik Cassel to build DynaBlocks, renamed Roblox.

links.took: Persistent cloud-hosted 3D worlds built and populated by users' own creations and avatars.
links.added: Simulated rigid-body block physics and game-creation tools aimed at kids and teens.
